title: Why are we all so stressed?
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是英国广播公司英文课的6分钟英语课

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. Worrying about work or exams, War and climate change in the news.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔 我是贝卡 担心工作或考试 战争和气候变化

sentences.en: It's no wonder that modern life is stressful.
sentences.zh: 难怪现代生活压力很大

sentences.en: What makes you stress, Neil? Oh, good question.
sentences.zh: 什么让你压力大了,尼尔?

sentences.en: I think not having enough time to do something, that really makes me stressed out.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没有足够的时间做一些事情, 这真的让我压力很大。

sentences.en: How about you? Um. When I'm trying to do something that I've never tried before and I'm not very good at it, that makes me feel really stressed.
sentences.zh: 嗯,当我试图做一些 我从来没有尝试过的事情, 我并不擅长它, 这让我感到真正的压力。

sentences.en: I find that stressful, too. And how do you cope with stressful situations, Neil?
sentences.zh: 我也觉得压力很大,你是怎么应付压力的,尼尔?

sentences.en: Well, I try to slow down, uh, pause, take a breath and think, ‘at some point, probably later today, everything will be okay again.’ How about you?
sentences.zh: 我试着减速, 暂停一下, 喘口气想想, “也许今天晚些时候, 一切都会好起来的。”你呢?

sentences.en: Yeah, same. But in my mind, I'm telling myself that, ‘I will be better at what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 是的,我也是,但是在我脑海中,我告诉自己, “我会在做我该做的事上做得更好。

sentences.en: I just need to practise more.’ Hmm. Many young people who feel stressed about the modern world use the word overwhelm to describe their feelings.
sentences.zh: 我只是需要更多练习。 ”嗯。 许多对现代世界感到压力的年轻人用这个词来描述他们的感受。

sentences.en: And overwhelm was also the topic of a recent BBC World Service programme, What in the World.
sentences.zh: 英国广播公司最近的一个世界服务节目“什么在世界上”的主题是“压倒一切”。

sentences.en: Here's Iqra Farooq and Claudia Hammond. So, overwhelm is an emotional state where you are struggling with your current situation.
sentences.zh: 这是Iqra Farooq 和 Claudia Hammond 。 所以, 过度的情绪状态, 你正在为目前的状况而挣扎。

sentences.en: So, you might feel overloaded, you might feel you can't cope, and that might be a temporary thing, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 所以,你可能会感到超负荷, 你可能会觉得你无法应付, 这也许是暂时的,希望。

sentences.en: But if it's not in the longer term, if that becomes more of a kind of chronic kind of stress, then that might lead to burnout in the end.
sentences.zh: 但是,如果它不是在较长的时间, 如果这变得更 一种慢性的压力, 那么这可能导致 燃烧在最后。

sentences.en: Feeling overwhelmed and unable to cope with life can become chronic, meaning that it lasts for a long time.
sentences.zh: 感觉不堪重负 无法应付生命 可能会变成慢性病 意味着它会持续很长时间

sentences.en: Overwhelm can lead to burnout, mental or physical exhaustion caused by working too hard.
sentences.zh: 过度劳累会导致体力或精神耗竭,因为工作太辛苦。

sentences.en: So how can we manage the stress in our lives and feel happier and healthier?
sentences.zh: 那么,我们如何应对我们生活中的压力,如何感到更快乐和更健康?

sentences.en: That's what we'll be discussing in this episode, along with some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 以及一些有用的新词和新词

sentences.en: You'll find all the vocabulary from this episode on our website bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的网站bbclearing english. com上会找到这集里的所有词汇

sentences.en: But before we start, I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 但是在我们开始之前 我有个问题要问你 尼尔

sentences.en: One simple way of combating stress is taking time to rest.
sentences.zh: 消除压力的一个简单办法是休息。

sentences.en: So, according to research conducted by BBC presenter and psychologist Claudia Hammond, which activity is thought to be the most restful?
sentences.zh: 根据BBC主持人和心理学家Claudia Hammond的研究 认为哪项活动最令人心烦意乱?

sentences.en: Is it: a) reading for pleasure, b) walking in nature, or c) listening to music?
sentences.zh: 是:(a) 为快乐而阅读,(b) 在大自然中行走,还是(c) 听音乐?

sentences.en: Well, I think they're all quite relaxing, but I'm gonna guess b) walking in nature.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我想他们都相当放松, 但我要猜b) 走路在自然界。

sentences.en: I'm surprised, Neil! I know you love music.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶 尼尔 我知道你喜欢音乐

sentences.en: And we'll find out the answer later. One of the most stressful things facing many young people is exams.
sentences.zh: 很多年轻人面临的最紧张的事情之一就是考试

sentences.en: Here, Claudia Hammond offers some advice for managing exam stress to BBC World Service's What in the World: …particularly in the exam itself, if you feel stressed, then just knowing that you may well perform better while you're stressed, that this… it concentrates the mind, it sharpens and you know nerves sharpen your thinking and allow you to really do your best.
sentences.zh: 在这里,克劳迪娅·哈蒙德向英国广播公司世界服务社(BBC World Services)提供一些关于管理考试压力的建议:.特别是考试本身,如果你感到压力,那么只要知道你在压力下表现会更好,这...它会集中思想,它会尖锐,而且你知道神经会提高你的思维力, 让你真正地发挥自己的作用。

sentences.en: It's normal to feel nerves before an exam.
sentences.zh: 考试前感觉神经正常

sentences.en: Nerves is an informal word for worry or anxiety, but according to Claudia, nerves aren't necessarily bad.
sentences.zh: 神经是一个非正式的词 担心或焦虑, 但根据克劳迪娅, 神经不一定坏。

sentences.en: Yes, nerves can help concentrate the mind.
sentences.zh: 是的,神经可以帮助 集中精神。

sentences.en: The phrase concentrate or sharpen the mind means to think more clearly about something, like an actor or an athlete feeling nerves before a big performance can help them do their best.
sentences.zh: 这个词集中或尖锐的头脑 意味着要更清晰地思考 某事,比如一个演员 或运动员感觉神经 之前,一个大表演 可以帮助他们 做他们最好的。

sentences.en: Claudia recommends other ways to reduce stress as well.
sentences.zh: 克劳迪娅也建议其他方法来减轻压力

sentences.en: These include slowing down and accepting that it’s ok to be ‘good enough’ rather than always trying for perfection.
sentences.zh: 包括减速, 接受「足够好」, 而非总是追求完美,

sentences.en: Here, she shares more top tips with Iqra Farooq for BBC World Service’s What in the World: I guess it's - there's no one-size-fits-all as well, when it comes to this.
sentences.zh: 她与Iqra Farooq分享更多关于BBC世界服务(The World Service)的文章:我想,

sentences.en: So, if someone's listening and thinking, ‘I want some top tips on just feeling overwhelmed generally in my life,’ what would you say to them?
sentences.zh: 所以,如果有人在倾听和思考, “我要一些顶尖的提示,

sentences.en: So, first I would say accept that your to-do list is never going to end, it's always going to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以,首先,我要说接受你的待办事宜清单 永远不会结束, 它会永远存在。

sentences.en: So, even I know that might sound defeatist, but even if you get to the end of it today, tomorrow there will be something else on it.
sentences.zh: 所以,即使我知道这听起来可能 失败主义者, 但即使你得到它到今天的结束, 明天会有别的东西在上面。

sentences.en: And that's just life, and that is just signs of a busy life.
sentences.zh: 这就是生活, 这只是一个繁忙生活的征兆。

sentences.en: There are many ways to combat stress, not a one-size-fits-all solution.
sentences.zh: 消除压力有许多办法,而不是一刀切的解决办法。

sentences.en: The phrase, one-size-fits-all, describes trying to apply the same solution to many different problems.
sentences.zh: " 一刀切 " 这一短语描述了试图对许多不同的问题采用同样的解决办法。

sentences.en: Claudia's final piece of advice is don't worry too much about your to-do-list, the list of all the items you have to do.
sentences.zh: 克劳迪娅最后的建议是 不要太担心你的待办事宜清单 以及你需要做的所有项目清单

sentences.en: Why? Because it never ends. Every day there will be something new to add to the list.
sentences.zh: 为什么 因为它永远不会结束 每天都会有新的东西要加到名单上

sentences.en: So, why stress? Some good advice there, Neil.
sentences.zh: 那么,为什么压力呢?

sentences.en: I think I'll try these techniques next time I feel stressed.
sentences.zh: 我想下次我感到压力的时候 我会试试这些技巧

sentences.en: And, speaking of ways to de-stress reminds me of my question I asked you earlier.
sentences.zh: 谈到解压的方法 让我想起我之前问你的问题

sentences.en: According to research conducted by BBC presenter and psychologist Claudia Hammond, which activity is thought of to be the most restful?
sentences.zh: 根据BBC主持人和心理学家Claudia Hammond的研究 认为哪项活动最令人焦虑?

sentences.en: And you answered b) walking in nature. Unfortunately, Neil, the answer is a) reading.
sentences.zh: 你回答b) 自然行走。不幸的是,尼尔,答案是a)阅读。

sentences.en: Ah well, reading is really relaxing as well.
sentences.zh: 读书也很轻松

sentences.en: OK, let’s recap the vocabulary from this episode, beginning with the adjective chronic, which means continuing for a long time.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下这集的词汇, 首先从形容词慢性开始, 这意味着要持续很长一段时间。

sentences.en: Burnout is a feeling of physical or mental exhaustion caused by working too hard.
sentences.zh: 烧伤是一种因工作太辛苦而导致的身体或精神疲劳的感觉。

sentences.en: If you say that a difficult situation sharpens or concentrates someone's mind, you mean that it makes them think clearly.
sentences.zh: 如果你说一个困难的情况 尖锐或集中 某人的头脑, 你的意思是,它让他们 思考清楚。

sentences.en: Nerves are an informal word for worry or anxiety.
sentences.zh: 神经是一个非正式的词 担心或焦虑。

sentences.en: A one-size-fits-all approach tries to apply the same solution to all problems, rather than solving them individually.
sentences.zh: " 一刀切 " 的办法试图对所有问题采用同样的解决办法,而不是单独解决这些问题。

sentences.en: And finally, a to-do list is a list of all the tasks you have to do.
sentences.zh: 最后,一个待办事宜列表 是一份您必须完成的所有任务的列表 。

sentences.en: Of course, another way to beat stress is doing something you love - and if that’s improving your English then why not visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you’ll find loads more activities for doing just that!
sentences.zh: 当然, 另一种克服压力的方法是做你喜欢的事情, 如果这能改善你的英语, 那么为什么不访问我们的网站,

sentences.en: See you again next time, but for now it’s goodbye!
sentences.zh: 下次再见,

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
